stemMd: A cabinet can be opened only if both a code and a key are available. The key is available, but the code is not. What follows?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The code becomes available whenever the key is present.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The cabinet can be opened because one condition is met.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The cabinet cannot be opened under the stated rule.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The cabinet can be opened only at night.

explanationMd: “Only if both” makes the conjunction of code and key a necessary condition. A missing code makes that conjunction false, so opening is ruled out. Possessing one necessary component is not enough to satisfy a requirement for both.

distractorRationale.b: Both conditions are necessary, not either one alone.
distractorRationale.e: The absence of the code does not imply a defective key.
distractorRationale.a: The premises explicitly say the code is absent.
